original.reason: It does not exclude the possible endpoints a and b from the equivalence class. The arguments only treat z<a and z>b; additional use of openness is needed to show an endpoint belonging to O would permit extending the interval and contradicting infimum/supremum.

judgment.reason: From z belonging to the defining set it concludes z>a (and analogously z<b), but membership alone gives only z>=a. Openness must be used to extend the interval past z.
It correctly establishes that classes are open intervals, explicitly using openness to rule out finite endpoints in a class, and injects the disjoint classes into Q.

The openness assertion in the converse supplies the needed endpoint exclusion: an open neighborhood of z extends the relevant closed interval past z. The remaining partition and rational-countability argument is correct.
It correctly uses openness to strengthen z>=a and z<=b to strict inequalities, identifies the equivalence classes as open intervals, and proves countability via distinct rationals.
